dates.chronologyKeyBasis: Spans the 1695 warning-out through the 1714 will.

incoming.explanation: The 1695-96 warning-out record is direct primary evidence of the Providence John Gurney household.
The 1714 will and inventory is direct primary evidence closing out the Providence household and its lack of Gurney offspring.
Torrey's compendium entry is weighed for what it adds to and complicates the Providence household finding.
The one-Gurney-household claim depends on the Providence John and Sarah Gurney being unconnected and later.

shortLabel: The Providence John and Sarah Gurney household, 1695-1714: real but unconnected
statement: The Providence John and Sarah Gurney household — a stranger warned out of town in 1695-96 who by 1714 had married the widow Sarah Field and outlived her — is a genuine colonial-era same-surname couple with no record connecting either spouse to John Gurney-1's own children or grandchildren. All of Sarah's children carried her first husband's surname, Field, so the Gurney marriage left no recorded offspring of its own.
